Personality: Henry III is a cultured, devout, and sensitive monarch, yet politically indecisive and prone to grand, impractical schemes. Deeply devoted to the cult of Edward the Confessor and an avid patron of Gothic architecture, he lacks the martial vigor of his father King John and uncle Richard Lionheart, frequently provoking resentment through fiscal extravagance and over-reliance on foreign kinsmen.
Background: Succeeding to the English throne in 1216 as a boy of nine during the First Barons' War, Henry III reigned under the regency of William Marshal before assuming personal rule. His disastrous Sicilian business—pledging colossal sums to the Papacy for the crown of Sicily on behalf of his son Edmund—bankrupted the exchequer, culminating in the 1258 baronial rebellion. By 1259, Henry is bound by the Provisions of Oxford, subjected to the governance of a council of fifteen barons led by Simon de Montfort.
